memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If anyone with malice aforethought shoves another or throws something at them intentionally so that they die or if out of enmity one person hits another with their fist so that the other dies, that person is to be put to death; that person is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death when they meet.'" - Num 35:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God continues to distinguish between accidental death and deliberate killing, and the key factor is the heart. "With malice aforethought... intentionally... out of enmity" — these phrases point to what was going on inside the person. It was not only the outward act that mattered but the intent behind it. God's justice looks past mere appearances to the motives of the heart.

This is a striking reminder that God sees the heart. We humans tend to judge by outward actions, but the Lord looks deeper. He weighs our intentions, our motives, the hidden attitudes that drive our behaviour. Two people might do the same outward thing, but with entirely different hearts, and God sees the difference clearly. As Scripture says, people look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart (1 Sam 16:7).

This should both humble us and comfort us. It humbles us because we cannot hide our true motives from God. We may fool others, and even ourselves, but He knows what is really going on inside. The malice, the enmity, the hidden bitterness — He sees it all. This calls us to honesty and to seek pure hearts before Him.

But it also comforts us, because God is not fooled by false appearances of guilt either. He judges rightly, according to truth. And for those in Christ, our hearts — though still imperfect — have been cleansed and are being made new. God sees us in His Son, and He is at work purifying our motives by His Spirit. Ask Him today to search your heart and lead you in His way (Ps 139:23-24), trusting the One who sees and judges rightly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there hidden motives in your heart that you need to bring before God?
2. How does knowing God sees the heart affect the way you live?
3. How does it comfort you that God judges rightly, according to truth?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see my heart and know my true motives. Cleanse me from hidden malice and bitterness, and make my heart pure before You. Thank You that in Christ I am being made new from the inside out. Amen.
